title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 19
paragraphs: Xerxes, now eager to undertake the expedition, afterwards saw a third vision in his sleep, which, when the Magi heard it, they interpreted as a sign that he would rule the whole earth and that all men would be subject to him. The vision was this: Xerxes dreamed that he had been crowned with a wreath of olive-branch, and that the shoots growing from the olive tree covered the whole earth; and after that the wreath, placed as it was on his head, disappeared. When the Magi had thus interpreted the dream, every one of the Persians who had been assembled there went back to his own province and set to the task of carrying out the commands with all zeal, each one eager to win for himself the gifts that had been offered. So Xerxes was gathering his army together, combing every region of the continent.
